---
title: Parameterization of the neighbor search
author: Aaron Lun
---

Let's see how the **nenesub** method behaves with respect to $k$ and $m$.

```{r}
set.seed(999)
x <- matrix(runif(10000), nrow=10)
length(nenesub::compute(x, 20, 10)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/20
length(nenesub::compute(x, 20, 5)) / ncol(x)
length(nenesub::compute(x, 10, 5)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/10
length(nenesub::compute(x, 5, 2)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/5
length(nenesub::compute(x, 50, 10)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/50
length(nenesub::compute(x, 50, 20)) / ncol(x)
```

So, the subsampling rate is comparable to $k$, though this breaks down at extreme $m$:

```{r}
length(nenesub::compute(x, 20, 20)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/20
length(nenesub::compute(x, 20, 1)) / ncol(x)
length(nenesub::compute(x, 10, 10)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/10
length(nenesub::compute(x, 10, 1)) / ncol(x)
```

We get similar results with different distributions and numbers of cells:

```{r}
set.seed(9999)
x <- matrix(rnorm(10000), nrow=5)
length(nenesub::compute(x, 20, 10)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/20
length(nenesub::compute(x, 20, 5)) / ncol(x)
length(nenesub::compute(x, 10, 5)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/10
length(nenesub::compute(x, 5, 2)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/5
length(nenesub::compute(x, 50, 10)) / ncol(x) # expect 1/50
length(nenesub::compute(x, 50, 20)) / ncol(x)
```
